_comment: The third paragraph of an expanded card: the explanation.
natal    what that part of you is        12, angles included
tone     what that kind of angle does     5
transit  how long it lasts, and why      10
── The `area` table is gone, and why ──
There used to be a fourth table here, keyed area by tone, and it supplied
paragraph two. It was written when the card body was a single 130
character sentence and the expansion had to carry the actual reading.
That made it a restatement by construction. An area's paragraph and an
area's opening were the same address, so the expansion paraphrased the
card it was expanding. Worst case, work by pull, shared every content
word with the opening printed directly above it: 'One of them pays and
one of them matters; today they want opposite hours' expanded to 'One of
them pays and one of them matters, and today they want opposite hours.'
And it was not bad luck. An aspect's area is derived from where the natal
point sits, so the two keys are correlated, and for the two angles they
are locked: the Ascendant is always the first sector and the Midheaven
always the tenth. Every Midheaven card ever rendered paired the midheaven
clause with a work opening and a work paragraph. Three tables, one
address, three paraphrases of one sentence.
The body is now the whole reading, written per area, tone and variant, so
there is nothing left for an area paragraph to add. The expansion goes:
1  the reading   what today is, and what to do about it  (readings.json)
2  the point     which part of you took it               (touches.json)
3  the mechanism which points, what angle, how long      (this file)
Paragraph three is allowed to sound like an explanation, because it is
one, and it is marked as one by sitting last under two that are not.
No proper nouns. Not one of these names a planet, because the card prints
the planet from the chart and a line that named it could be wrong. The
same rule governs readings.json, touches.json and signs.json.

natal.sun: This is the part of you that wants to be recognised as itself. When something lands on it, the day turns on being seen accurately, and being seen wrongly costs more than it usually would.
natal.moon: This is the part that reacts before you have decided anything. It sets the weather of a day a few minutes ahead of your reasoning, which is why the mood arrives first and the explanation second.
natal.mercury: This is the part that turns a thought into a sentence. Angles to it show up in the wording of things rather than in what you meant, which is why a good point can land badly on one of these days.
natal.venus: This is the part that decides what you are drawn to and what is worth having. Angles to it show up in what you want, which is not always the same as what you then do about it.
natal.mars: This is where the push comes from. Angles to it show up as speed, appetite and irritation, usually in that order and usually before you have chosen a target for any of them.
natal.jupiter: This is the part that wants more room. Angles to it widen whatever they touch, and they are not selective about it: the opportunity and the overreach arrive together.
natal.saturn: This is what asks for patience and keeps the promises. Angles to it feel heavy even when nothing has actually gone wrong, and they reward doing the dull thing on time.
natal.uranus: This is the part that will not stay put. Angles to it arrive abruptly and rarely at a convenient hour, and the urge they produce is usually right about the need and wrong about the target.
natal.neptune: This is where the edges go soft. Angles to it make the story you are telling yourself more persuasive and the facts harder to get at, in both directions at once.
natal.pluto: This is what will not be negotiated. Angles to it do not adjust things, they change them, which is why they are uncomfortable long before they are useful.
natal.ascendant: This is not a planet. It is the degree that was climbing over the horizon at the minute you were born, which is why it fixes the whole sector layout, and why an angle to it shows up in how you land on a room before it shows up in anything you do.
natal.midheaven: This is not a planet either. It is the degree that was directly overhead when you were born, the highest point the sky reached, and it stands for the part of a life other people can see from a distance: the standing, the reputation, the answer to what it is you do.

tone.charged: This is a conjunction: two bodies in the same degree. It does not pull in a direction, it amplifies whatever was already running, which is why it is the easiest angle to notice and the hardest to give advice about.
tone.open: This is a soft angle, and an opening rather than a push. Nothing here forces itself on the day. It is available, and it stays available only while the angle holds.
tone.friction: This is a hard angle between two parts of a chart that both want the day. It does not resolve by picking a winner. It resolves by doing the smaller, duller thing that neither part objects to.
tone.easy: This is the easiest angle there is, and it costs nothing, which is exactly its risk. What runs clean tends to run unattended, and a day like this can pass without the ease having been spent on anything.
tone.pull: This puts two parts of your chart at opposite ends of one line. Both are real and both are yours. The work is not picking one, it is admitting the trade rather than pretending there is not one.

transit.moon: The body making this angle covers thirteen degrees a day, so the contact forms and breaks inside a few hours. Whatever it is doing, it is not doing it tomorrow.
transit.sun: The body making this angle moves about a degree a day, so this is a matter of two or three days rather than an afternoon, and it comes round once a year.
transit.mercury: The body making this angle moves roughly a degree a day and turns back on itself more often than anything else, so contacts from it are short and can repeat within a season.
transit.venus: The body making this angle takes a few days over it. Long enough to be a mood rather than a moment, short enough that waiting it out is a real option.
transit.mars: The body making this angle takes the better part of a week, which is long enough for a mood to turn into a decision if nobody interrupts it.
transit.jupiter: The body making this angle takes about a month to cross, so this is a season of something rather than a day of it, and there is no need to act on the first morning.
transit.saturn: The body making this angle moves a couple of degrees a year, so this has been forming for months and will take months to clear. Nothing about it is sudden and nothing about it is precise.
transit.uranus: The body making this angle moves slowly and arrives abruptly, so the contact spans months while the things that happen inside it do not.
transit.neptune: The body making this angle covers less than a degree in a season, so this is a long, undramatic weather system rather than a day, and it clears the same way it arrived.
transit.pluto: The body making this angle covers about two arcseconds a day, so this contact spans seasons and can return two or three times before it is finished. It is the slowest thing on this page by a wide margin.
